newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LG-Caltex targets max output on new CDU by Nov 23.
newsitem.headline: LG-Caltex targets max output on new CDU by Nov 23.

text.p: South Korea's LG-Caltex Oil Corp, a unit of the LG Group, expects full production of its new crude distillation unit (CDU) by November 23, a senior LG-Caltex official said on Thursday.
The new CDU has a government licensed production capacity of 220,000 barrels per day (bpd), but company officials said the unit will be capable of processing 270,000 bpd of crude oil.
"We plan to start feeding the crude in on November 16 and expect the unit to run at full capacity in one week's period," the official at the LG-Caltex's refinery in Yeochon told Reuters.
The new CDU has been mechanically completed and it is currently going through final checks for possible leaks and pressure.
The official said LG-Caltex would rely on light and sweet crude oil as the feed for the new unit.
He said the refiner is aiming for a product mix of 25 percent liquefied petroleum gas and naphtha, 45 percent middle distillates and 30 percent fuel oil.
The new unit will boost LG-Caltex's licensed crude processing capacity to 600,000 bpd from the current 380,000 bpd to debut as the nation's second largest refiner.
South Korea currently has a refining capability of 2.22 million bpd.
LG-Caltex is a joint venture between LG Group and Caltex Petroleum Corp, itself a joint venture between U.S. oil giants Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
